newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA STATE BANK BCR TO LAUNCH EUROBONDS IN FEB.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA STATE BANK BCR TO LAUNCH EUROBONDS IN FEB.

text.p: Romanian state bank Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) said on Tuesday it would launch a three-year Eurobond issue later this month, through Merrill Lynch International.

The amount and terms of the dollar-denominated issue -- the first non-government guaranteed raising by a Romanian corporate -- will be set after a 10-day road show in Paris, Zurich, London, New York and Frankfurt, a BCR statement said.
It did not give the destination of the raising.
Last year, BCR president Ion Ghica said his bank planned to raise between $60 million and $100 million from international capital markets early in 1997.
The BCR, which specialised in industry financing before the 1989 fall of communism, was reshaped in December 1990. It continues to manage the bulk of loans going to industry.
The bank, boasting one of the strongest networks in Romania, has a share capital of 225.4 billion lei, with assets at 4.7 trillion lei.

Moody's Investors Service assigned BCR last month a B1 and Not-Prime for long- and short-term deposits, and a D bank financial strength rating. Its rating for short-term local currency debt, awarded by Thomson BankWatch, is LC1.
Merrill Lynch helped Romania last year rejoin the world capital market after more than a decade of isolation imposed by the ousted communist regime of late dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
It advised Romania in getting its first credit ratings last year, and said it would help it upgrade further its scores.
Romania has a BB-plus score by Japan Credit Rating agency, little higher than the BB- minus ratings of Standard and Poors and IBCA, and the BA-three from Moody's.
Merrill Lynch is also arranging the first foreign issue by a Romanian city helping Bucharest raise up to $200 million in a private placement and in bonds to upgrade infrastructure. ($=6,464 lei)
